course.title: Python Programming MOOC 2026
course.provider: University of Helsinki (Department of Computer Science, MOOC Center)
course.format: self-paced, 14 parts; Introduction to Programming (BSCS1001, parts 1-7, 5 ECTS) + Advanced Course in Programming (BSCS1002, parts 8-14, 5 ECTS); auto-graded TMC exercises, Zoom lectures, exams
course.notes: Edition: 2026 (programming-26.mooc.fi, open until end of 2026); the 2025 edition (programming-25.mooc.fi) has an identical part/section structure. The site labels parts only by number ('Part 1'...'Part 14'); module titles here are composed from the official section titles, which are listed verbatim in `topics`. Section titles and exercise names were taken from the course's public source repo (rage/programming-26). `projects` lists a selection of notable/multi-part exercises, not every exercise (each part has ~15-40 exercises). Part 14 is a pygame game project (a Sokoban-style 'robot and boxes' worked example, then a peer-reviewed game of the student's own). Part 1-3 exercises run in an in-browser editor; VS Code + TMC plugin are introduced in part 4. Concept depth is a judgement from section content/exercise counts. 'polymorphism' is only implicit (method overriding in part 10), not named as such; 'math_module' is used in part 1 (sqrt for quadratic equation) but modules are formally taught in part 7. Not covered: sets as a topic, enumerate/zip, unit testing (tests are run by TMC but not taught), dataclasses, decorators beyond @property/@classmethod. New concept IDs: conditional_expressions, event_driven_programming.

modules.title: Part 1: Getting started, input, variables, arithmetic and conditionals
Part 2: Programming terminology, more conditionals, combining conditions and simple loops
Part 3: Loops with conditions, working with strings, more loops and defining functions
Part 4: VS Code and debugger, more functions, lists, definite iteration, formatting, strings and lists
topics: The Visual Studio Code editor, Python interpreter and built-in debugging tool

modules.title: Part 5: More lists, references, dictionaries and tuples
projects: Sudoku (check row/column/block/grid, print grid, add number)

modules.title: Part 6: Reading and writing files, handling errors, local and global variables
Part 7: Modules, randomness, times and dates, data processing, own modules, more Python features
Part 8: Objects and methods, classes and objects, defining classes and methods
Part 9: Objects and references, objects as attributes, encapsulation, method scope, class attributes
Part 10: Class hierarchies, access modifiers, OOP techniques, developing a larger application
Part 11: List comprehensions, more comprehensions, recursion, more recursion examples
Part 12: Functions as arguments, generators, functional programming, regular expressions
Part 13: Pygame, animation, events, more pygame techniques
